ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) databases, the consolidated EU restrictive measures list (EU Sanctions Map), the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and Spanish domestic sanctions and criminal registries (SEPBLAC, Ministerio del Interior and Agencia Tributaria). Screening must be conducted continuously and documented under an AML/CFT policy compliant with Article 14 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online service for Certificación de Denominación Social via the official platform www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin characters. Non-Latin script names are transliterated into the Spanish alphabet. Names in Spanish or in any EU official language are accepted provided they are intelligible and not misleading under Article 145 of the Spanish Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital). The name must not coincide with any existing or reserved name in the Central Commercial Registry, and must appropriately identify the entity type as 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or its abbreviation 'S.L.' (or 'SL').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Banco de Crédito, Caja de Ahorros, Cooperativa de Crédito, Entidad de Dinero Electrónico, Entidad de Pago (financial entities requiring separate ministerial authorization)
Seguros, Reaseguros, Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (insurance/captive/insurance-reinsurance terms requiring DGSPP authorization)
Sociedad de Inversión, Fondo de Pensiones, Gestora de Fondos, Sociedad Gestora (collective investment institutions requiring CNMV authorization)
España, Estado, Ministerio, Administración Pública, Instituto Nacional, Consejo General (terms implying public, governmental or institutional character without special license)
Geographic names (e.g., particular Spanish cities/regions) if the registered office is not located there and no legitimate link exists

Professional designations (Abogado, Procurador, Médico, Arquitecto, Ingeniero, Auditor, etc.) unless the company demonstrates that at least one partner is a duly qualified and registered professional in that field
Words already reserved or incorporated in the Central Commercial Registry, including homophones and abbreviations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may file a new certification application with a corrected or alternative name. Where the refusal is based on subjective grounds (e.g., misleading or contrary to law), an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Directorate General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) within one month of the notification. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may initiate an administrative-litigation appeal before the Juzgado Central de lo Contencioso-Administrativo within two months. In parallel, the applicant may submit up to three alternative names in the same application to mitigate delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only as an administrative correspondence and service-reception address, provided that the registered office is a real physical location specified in the incorporation deed and accepted by the Mercantile Registry and the Tax Agency (AEAT). For a steel-structure prefab EPC business, the registered office must correspond to where the central administration or principal establishment is located; virtual offices will not satisfy commercial substance requirements for value-added tax (IVA), corporate tax presence, or construction-sector licensing, and are subject to challenge in tax audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate annual probability (approximately 10%–20%) for newly incorporated companies in the construction and engineering services sector, based on AEAT tax audit selection criteria, municipal commercial-substance checks, and occasional AML on-site inspections under Ley 10/2010. The risk increases where the registered office is a virtual office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – sede electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) incorporated in Spain, obtain a name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central; file Form 036 with AEAT to request the provisional NIF; execute the public incorporation deed before a notary and register the company in the Registro Mercantil; submit the definitive NIF application form to AEAT within 15 days of registration; complete the census declaration on Form 036/037 for VAT and Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas (IAE). Non-resident shareholder/officers must obtain their own NIF by attending AEAT in person or through a certified representative with power of attorney, passport and proof of address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply a US-style check-the-box election; the SL is automatically a resident corporate taxpayer, subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income. Optional tax elections include: consolidation as a fiscal group under articles 55–70 of Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (LIS) for groups meeting the 75% shareholding and other legal conditions; application of the reduced corporate tax rate for newly created SLs under article 29 LIS if the activity and turnover conditions are met; and special regimes such as patent box or ETVE that require formal election and AEAT approval. No hybrid mismatch check-the-box election exists; anti-hybrid rules under Law 11/2021 apply mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for resident Spanish entities; a taxable person must register for Spanish VAT before carrying out taxable activities. Non-established EU suppliers have a €10,000 annual distance-sales threshold for B2C supplies; B2B services are subject to reverse charge and no registration threshold applies. A non-EU supplier is registrable whenever it makes taxable supplies of goods or services in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not have a real-time disapprove/approval clearance model. The Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA (SII) is mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover above €6 million and certain other taxpayers; SII requires electronic forwarding of VAT invoice records to AEAT within 4 or 8 business days. The Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 impose mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and require billing software to comply with Veri*Factu standards, making invoice records available to AEAT. No digital stamping or central fiscal clearance is applied; however, immediate tax authority access to e-invoice records is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An export of goods to a destination outside the EU (including Ceuta/Melilla under article 21 Ley 37/1992) is exempt from VAT with full right to deduct input VAT if the goods physically leave the Spanish/EU customs territory and the taxpayer retains satisfactory evidence of export. The exporter must identify the destination, dispatch within the legal period, and submit a customs export declaration accepted by the customs authorities. Services benefiting from the export exemption must be directly related to exported goods or supplied to a non-established business/customer in a third country; the supplier must obtain documentary proof of the recipient's identity, establishment, and foreign destination to substantiate zero-rating. Input VAT recovery is conditional on correct invoicing and storage of the required evidence for at least four years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Administrativa / DUA-SAD)
Bill of Lading (B/L), airway bill, or CMR/international transport document evidencing the physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit confirmation of the export payment received from outside Spain
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the goods exported and the customs declaration
Proof of exit from EU customs territory, such as customs stamp, summary exit declaration, or external transit document
Intrastat filing (not required for non-EU exports but required for intra-EU dispatches)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT will scrutinise export evidence, transport timelines, the economic substance of the exporter, and receipt of foreign currency proceeds. If zero-rating is improperly claimed or the documentation is incomplete or false, AEAT may retroactively recharacterise the supply as taxable in Spain, assess the unpaid VAT plus late-interest penalties, and deny/reclaim input VAT refunds. Proportional penalties range from 50% to 150% of the deficient tax; where tax loss exceeds €120,000, criminal liability under article 305 of the Criminal Code may arise. Invoices and transport files must be retained for at least four years, and any subsequent failure to substantiate export status triggers clawback of the deducted input VAT and related interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-investment and certain cross-border reporting matters are administered by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and applies EU Treaty freedoms for capital movements and payments. The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, foreign-investment screening, and prudential rules. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign equity, shareholder loans, trade receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, and liquidation proceeds and remit them abroad through regulated payment institutions or banks. Profit remittance requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and the distribution resolution, satisfaction of statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules, and withholding-tax analysis. Dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, and related-party payments may require Spanish withholding, EU Parent-Subsidiary or Interest and Royalties Directive relief, treaty relief, beneficial-owner evidence, transfer-pricing support, and evidence that the recipient is not in a non-cooperative jurisdiction. Banks may require corporate resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, tax forms, and underlying contracts before processing remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for an exporter to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España, convert them into euros, or maintain them in a Spanish bank. Export receipts may generally remain in foreign currency or be credited to an eligible foreign account, subject to bank controls, accounting, tax, sanctions, and AML requirements. The company should retain invoices, customs or transport evidence where applicable, contracts, shipping documents, proof of delivery, and bank advices. Cross-border transaction, external-asset, foreign-investment, or statistical reports may apply when regulatory thresholds and reporting conditions are met; the applicable Banco de España and Ministry forms and thresholds should be checked for each reporting period. Physical movements of cash and certain bearer instruments of EUR 10,000 or more into or out of Spain require the applicable declaration. No mandatory export-receipt conversion ratio or universal statutory repatriation deadline applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for a supplementary operating account where the provider is an EU-authorised electronic money institution or payment institution, is lawfully passported or otherwise authorised to provide services in Spain, supports EUR SEPA payments, and accepts Spanish companies. Low for an offshore digital EMI without Spanish authorisation, EU passporting, a regulated EEA establishment, or a clear legal basis to provide payment services to a Spanish SL. EMI funds are safeguarded rather than treated as bank deposits and may not receive ordinary deposit-guarantee protection. Fintech access does not replace a Spanish bank account for all public-authority, notarial, payroll, lending, cash, or trade-finance requirements. Enhanced due diligence is common for non-resident owners, complex groups, high-value construction payments, crypto exposure, sanctioned-country links, and unexplained third-party receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal rule that all directors must attend a branch physically. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents, and electronic signatures, but the bank determines its procedure. At least one authorised representative, director, beneficial owner, or controlling person may be required to complete live video or in-person verification. Banks may require a Spanish address, Spanish tax identification number, original or apostilled documents, sworn translations, a branch meeting, or an in-person interview where ownership, source of funds, business substance, or foreign-control risk cannot be satisfactorily verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with incomplete identity, tax-residence, or ownership information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport or national identity document; Spanish NIE or applicable foreign tax identifier; current residential address evidence; tax-residence certificate; complete ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; corporate registry extracts; director and signatory powers; notarised or electronically verifiable corporate resolutions; apostille and sworn translation where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital, shareholder loans, or recurring inbound transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; bank statements showing originating funds; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; evidence of accumulated profits, sale proceeds, financing, or investment funds; board and shareholder approvals; tax filings where relevant; transaction-purpose explanation; beneficial-owner source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated steel-prefabrication business and expected payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; customer and supplier schedule; EPC, engineering, fabrication, and installation contracts; invoices and purchase orders; project pipeline; warehouse or premises evidence; website and commercial registrations; expected monthly volumes, countries, currencies, counterparties, and payment purposes; logistics and delivery documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unusual third-party payments, pass-through flows, cash deposits, or payments unrelated to invoiced construction activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual basis for each payment; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; third-party payment authorisation; customer or supplier KYC; proof of delivery or performance; accounting ledger; payment-flow diagram; written explanation of agency, subcontracting, factoring, or group-settlement arrangements; controls prohibiting unexplained third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Country, counterparty, sanctions, export-control, or politically exposed person exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening records; counterparty ownership files; end-use and end-user statements; origin and destination documentation; export-control classification; shipping and customs records; compliance policy; escalation and approval log; evidence of enhanced due diligence and refusal of prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex group structure, nominee ownership, holding-company layers, or beneficial ownership inconsistent with public filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full group chart; registry certificates for every relevant entity; constitutional documents; shareholder registers; trust or nominee declarations where applicable; UBO identification; intercompany agreements; rationale for each entity; tax-residence and substance evidence; legal opinion where ownership interpretation is material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, or related-party payment uncertainty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax identification; tax-residence certificates; treaty forms; related-party agreements; transfer-pricing policy and local file where required; withholding analysis; invoices and deliverables; board approvals; accounting treatment; evidence of arm's-length pricing and beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dormant or newly incorporated SL with no Spanish commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed and Commercial Registry evidence; registered office and operating-premises evidence; employee or contractor records where applicable; management and procurement plan; licences or permits if later required by project activity; projected cash flow; initial customer and supplier contracts; local accounting and tax adviser mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for foreign-currency accounts, frequent FX conversions, or high-volume international settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Currency exposure schedule; expected import and export flows; invoice currency matrix; treasury policy; approved counterparties; hedging rationale; bank statements; underlying commercial contracts; forecast volumes; documented segregation of operating, payroll, tax, and client-money flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity funding through a regulated Spanish or EEA bank to the SL's designated corporate account. For a new SL, use the bank's incorporation-capital process and obtain the bank certificate or electronic confirmation required by the notary and Commercial Registry; after incorporation, convert or replace the temporary account with the operating account. Record equity increases through the required shareholder and notarial resolutions and Commercial Registry filing. Route shareholder loans under a signed loan agreement with principal, maturity, interest, repayment, transfer-pricing, and withholding provisions. The remitter should be the shareholder or documented group treasury entity, not an unrelated third party. Use the bank's correct purpose and payment reference, such as equity contribution, capital increase, shareholder loan, or intercompany financing; Spain does not impose one universal public purpose-code list for ordinary commercial wires. Provide UBO, source-of-funds, transaction documents, tax-residence evidence, and foreign-investment information where applicable. Reconcile the incoming transfer to the accounting ledger and preserve MT103 or equivalent payment evidence. Screen all banks, remitters, beneficiaries, and jurisdictions against EU and Spanish sanctions and AML requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA where speed, cost, and beneficiary acceptance are suitable. Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA or foreign-currency wires, with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, purpose, invoice, and intermediary-bank information. For supplier or project risk, use a documentary commercial letter of credit, including irrevocable LC, confirmed LC, standby LC, or bank guarantee as commercially appropriate; specify governing rules such as UCP 600 or ISP98, required shipping and performance documents, discrepancy procedures, expiry, sanctions wording, and reimbursement mechanics. Use documentary collections only where counterparty risk is acceptable. For each payment retain purchase order, contract, invoice, customs or transport evidence where relevant, goods-receipt or works-completion evidence, VAT treatment, approval record, and payment reconciliation. Do not use personal accounts, anonymous payment providers, unlicensed offshore platforms, crypto rails, or unrelated third-party accounts for ordinary trade settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm for documented commercial exposures, subject to MiFID II classification, appropriateness or suitability procedures where applicable, collateral terms, confirmation controls, valuation, accounting, and EMIR reporting or exemption analysis.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, provided the product is lawfully offered by the counterparty, the reference rate and settlement currency are defined, the transaction hedges a genuine exposure, and sanctions, local exchange-control, EMIR, and counterparty-risk requirements are satisfied.

Cross-currency swaps or currency swaps for documented multi-period funding or operating exposures, with approved ISDA or equivalent documentation, confirmation of principal exchanges and interest flows, collateral and close-out terms, valuation controls, and EMIR reporting or clearing analysis.

FX options, collars, and participating forwards may be used for documented commercial exposures where the bank confirms product legality, risk disclosures, accounting treatment, and corporate-authority requirements; avoid speculative or leveraged structures outside the approved treasury policy.

Use a board-approved treasury policy establishing permitted currencies, hedge ratios, authorised counterparties, credit limits, segregation of dealing and settlement, confirmations, independent valuation, hedge-accounting documentation, collateral management, liquidity stress testing, and prohibition of uncovered speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Cuentas Anuales – Depósito de Cuentas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office (Registro Mercantil provincial / Central)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by shareholders’ meeting within 6 months of fiscal year end (by 30 June for calendar year); filing within 1 month after approval (30 July standard for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under Regulation (EU) 2015/1880: EUR 200 (1–3 months), EUR 400 (3–6 months), EUR 800 (6–12 months), EUR 1,500 (>12 months); continued non-filing triggers closing of the registry sheet, preventing registration of any further corporate transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades – Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration (AEAT – Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 calendar days after six months following the tax year end (for calendar year: 25 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on delay plus late interest; formal penalty of EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 for inaccurate or omitted data; administrative strike-off not applicable to tax filings but enforced through execution of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real – integrated in annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as annual accounts deposit: approval by 30 June, filing by 30 July for calendar year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Anti-money laundering fines under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014: EUR 10,000 to EUR 60,000 for serious breaches; EUR 60,000 to EUR 300,000 or up to 10% of net turnover for very serious infractions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders’ General Meeting Approval of Accounts and Budget
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 6 months of each fiscal year end (no later than 30 June for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to call the meeting invalidates the annual accounts filing; directors may be liable for unaudited depreciation of corporate assets; company may be audited or subject to judicial dissolution for grave management defaults

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 January following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal penalty of EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 depending on nature and volume; late filing of complete summary can result in EUR 1,000 penalty; failure may block export and contracting certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February of the following year (standard: 1 February to 28 February/29 February in leap years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 200 to EUR 300 per omitted or inaccurate record, subject to minimum scale; if triggered by requests in advance, penalty up to EUR 20,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required if, for two consecutive years, an SL meets at least two: (i) total assets exceed EUR 3,650,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 7,300,000; (iii) average headcount exceeds 50 employees. Below these thresholds, audit is voluntary and exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable – PGC) under Real Decreto 1514/2007; IFRS-EU adopted for consolidated accounts and optionally for individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SL must maintain an updated register of ultimate beneficial owners (Registro de Titularidad Real) and re-confirm it at the time of filing annual accounts. Any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the company's internal share register (Libro Registro de Socios) and the updated ownership particulars reported in the annual UBO filing; non-compliance triggers AML penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titularidad Real)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,500 – EUR 8,000 (USD 2,700 – 8,600) for a small/medium SL; consolidated or large entities from EUR 10,000 to EUR 25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created entities (LIS art. 29.1) applied in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base where an economic activity is effectively conducted; 15% rate for qualifying emerging start-up companies (Ley 28/2022) for the first four tax periods; patent box exemption of 50% of qualifying IP income (art. 23 LIS); R&D&I tax credit of 25% of qualified research expenditure and 8% of technological innovation expenditure; reinvestment relief under art. 42 LIS allowing 50% exemption of certain capital gains; SME reserve of leveling (reserva de nivelación) permitting a 10% reduction of the taxable base subject to a 5-year retention requirement.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; no statutory expiry under LIS art. 26. General annual offset cap of 25% of the taxable base; taxpayers with annual net turnover below EUR 1 million may offset up to 100% of the taxable base; taxpayers with net turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million may offset the first EUR 1 million without cap plus 25% of the excess; taxpayers with net turnover of at least EUR 20 million are subject to the 25% cap on the full taxable base.
